items.title: Capability-policy states lack a transition and precedence contract
items.statement: The GUI state vocabulary and global/per-project scopes are listed, but the core does not define legal transitions, inheritance precedence, conflict detection, optimistic concurrency, or the result of authority revocation while Auto or On work is active.
items.impact: Concurrent edits or revocation can produce divergent effective policy and misleading completion eligibility.

evidence.exact_quote: Testing capability policy is implementation-ready only when the GUI exposes concrete controls and receipts, not merely policy prose. The production GUI must provide global and per-project rows for each capability family with inherited/effective state, `Auto`, `On`, `Off`, unavailable, blocked-needs-authority, and prohibited-by-policy projections. `Auto` may discover/select/install within authority; `On` blocks or asks for authority when unavailable; `Off` prohibits use and installation and never counts as successful verification.

items.title: Auto installation has no destructive-action or rollback contract
items.statement: Auto is allowed to install within authority, but there is no preview, package/source trust rule, filesystem scope, cancellation point, rollback/uninstall behavior, or cleanup receipt for a failed or partially completed installation.
items.impact: A capability probe can leave project or host state mutated even when verification never becomes usable.

evidence.exact_quote: Testing capability policy is implementation-ready only when the GUI exposes concrete controls and receipts, not merely policy prose. The production GUI must provide global and per-project rows for each capability family with inherited/effective state, `Auto`, `On`, `Off`, unavailable, blocked-needs-authority, and prohibited-by-policy projections. `Auto` may discover/select/install within authority; `On` blocks or asks for authority when unavailable; `Off` prohibits use and installation and never counts as successful verification.

items.title: Testing commands omit actor, authorization, idempotency, and ordering semantics
items.statement: Required commands promise evidence links but do not require actor or authority refs, request/idempotency keys, causal sequence, prior-state version, duplicate suppression, or replay behavior.
items.impact: Retries or multiple controllers can open duplicate sessions, overwrite policy, or produce receipts that cannot prove who authorized the action.

evidence.exact_quote: The required command rows are `cmd.testing.capability_policy.set`, `cmd.testing.visibility_policy.set`, `cmd.testing.session.open`, `cmd.testing.session.watch`, `cmd.testing.session.background`, and `cmd.testing.session.redaction.inspect`. Each command must produce receipt evidence linked to the effective policy snapshot, visible-session identity, artifact/evidence refs, redaction profile, currentness/revalidation result, and fallback route when a visual surface cannot be embedded.

items.title: Redaction authorization and evidence lifecycle are under-specified
items.statement: The redaction-failure exception names an owning policy but does not define who may authorize it, purpose and scope limits, expiry/revocation, immutable audit evidence, recipient visibility, retention, deletion, or propagation to already persisted copies.
items.impact: Sensitive screenshots, logs, or traces could be displayed or retained indefinitely under an ambiguous override.

evidence.exact_quote: Screenshots, videos, logs, console output, network traces, and artifact previews apply secret and sensitive-data redaction before display or persistence. Redaction failures block display/persistence until resolved or explicitly authorized by the owning policy; they do not silently downgrade evidence quality.

items.title: Project-native harness commands are not treated as untrusted execution
items.statement: Harness probing records runnable commands and adapters, but the core defines no sandbox, working-directory boundary, environment or secret policy, path validation, network/host authority, resource limits, or provenance check before those commands run.
items.impact: A malicious or compromised repository can turn discovery and testing into arbitrary host execution or secret exfiltration.

evidence.exact_quote: Test Capability Discovery must run before test generation or execution. It detects project_platform, framework/toolkit, local_capabilities, installed tools, app launch ability, browser automation, GUI automation, device/emulator automation, screenshot support, logs, headless/headed support, project-native test runners, and whether current official testing options need online research. Test Harness Probe records runnable verification commands, required adapters, expected artifacts, flake policy, and gaps before Executor treats a WorkNode request as test-ready.

items.title: Partial test runs have no atomicity, cancellation, or resume model
items.statement: TestRunReceipt fields are listed, but there is no run state machine for queued/running/cancelled/timed-out/crashed/partially-collected outcomes, no rule for committing a receipt and artifacts atomically, and no resume or cleanup semantics.
items.impact: A crash can leave evidence that appears complete, orphaned artifacts, or duplicate resumed runs with conflicting verdicts.

evidence.exact_quote: Automated completion means 100% automated verification with no human intervention for required browser/GUI/device sessions; Playwright optional remains fallback/project-native, and manual_only_acceptance_not_allowed blocks manual-only completion claims. TestRunReceipt records include receipt_id, test_strategy_ref, test_case_refs, generated_test_ids, reused_test_ids, verification_command, expected_artifacts, evidence_refs, visual_evidence_refs, flake_policy, and test_gap_policy.

items.title: Flake policy lacks falsifiable retry and quarantine rules
items.statement: The strategy and receipt carry a flake policy, but the core does not define retry budgets, independence requirements, seed capture, pass thresholds, quarantine expiry, known-failure handling, or whether a retry pass may certify completion.
items.impact: Repeated retries can convert nondeterminism into a false pass without a reproducible oracle.

evidence.exact_quote: Required automated-testing data shapes include project platform and framework/toolkit identity, local capability inventory, online research requirement, harness probe command and adapter results, required capability refs, generated or reused test IDs, browser/session requirements, visual evidence requirements, expected artifacts, flake policy, test oracle selection, and test-gap policy.

items.title: Online research dependency has no offline or network-loss outcome
items.statement: Discovery can decide current official options need online research, but the authoritative core does not say whether network denial, mid-request loss, stale cached knowledge, or partial research blocks capability status, degrades it, or permits a bounded fallback.
items.impact: Identical projects can receive inconsistent readiness decisions depending on transient connectivity.

evidence.exact_quote: TestCapabilityReport and TestHarnessProbeReport fields include online_research, automation_surface, requires_browser, requires_emulator, requires_display, requires_screenshot, verification_command, expected_artifacts, and flake_policy.

items.title: Evidence capture has no scale, quota, or backpressure limits
items.statement: The required visual and telemetry streams have no maximum size or duration, concurrency limit, pagination rule, sampling policy, retention quota, eviction priority, or producer backpressure behavior.
items.impact: Long or parallel sessions can exhaust disk, memory, UI rendering capacity, or artifact transport while still being required for certification.

evidence.exact_quote: Visible testing projections must include `show_when_possible`, visible active, collapsed, detached, backgrounded, and non-embeddable states. Web evidence must show browser navigation, clicks, form input, assertions, screenshots, console, network, and pass/fail progression where supported. Native evidence must show Swift/live preview, hot reload, simulator, emulator, physical device stream, application window, interaction trace, screenshots, and logs where available and permitted.

items.title: Testing controls and evidence viewers lack accessibility acceptance criteria
items.statement: Desktop test strategy mentions accessibility checks for tested applications, but the production testing GUI itself has no keyboard, focus, screen-reader, contrast, reduced-motion, zoom, transcript, or non-visual evidence requirements.
items.impact: Users relying on assistive technology may be unable to configure policies or interpret test status and evidence.

evidence.exact_quote: Test Strategy v2 binds each WorkNode request to required_capability_refs, required harnesses, generated or reused tests, generated_test_ids, reused_test_ids, completion commands, browser/session requirements, emulator requirements, visual evidence requirements, expected artifacts, flake policy, and test_gap_policy. The strategy must choose project-type-specific oracles: browser DOM, console, network, screenshot, and visual checks for web; launch, window, screenshot, and accessibility checks for desktop GUI; emulator/device logs and screenshots for mobile; API, contract, and database checks for backend work; exit, output, and filesystem checks for CLI work; and unit, property, and API contracts for libraries.

items.title: Visible testing states have no localization contract
items.statement: The GUI requires many user-visible state and remediation labels, but the core gives no locale fallback, message-key/parameter contract, expansion or truncation handling, bidirectional layout behavior, timestamp/number formatting, or localization test oracle.
items.impact: Translated status can be clipped, ambiguous, or incorrectly formatted, especially for security- and authority-sensitive states.

evidence.exact_quote: Testing capability policy is implementation-ready only when the GUI exposes concrete controls and receipts, not merely policy prose. The production GUI must provide global and per-project rows for each capability family with inherited/effective state, `Auto`, `On`, `Off`, unavailable, blocked-needs-authority, and prohibited-by-policy projections. `Auto` may discover/select/install within authority; `On` blocks or asks for authority when unavailable; `Off` prohibits use and installation and never counts as successful verification.

items.title: Testing artifacts have no versioning or migration semantics
items.statement: The design-only artifact families are named without schema/version discriminators, compatibility negotiation, unknown-field policy, migration ownership, legacy receipt interpretation, or rules for revalidating evidence after a schema or adapter upgrade.
items.impact: Persisted strategies and receipts can become unreadable or, worse, be interpreted under newer semantics and falsely certify work.

evidence.exact_quote: Automated testing contracts are represented in `Plans/plans_to_code_handoff.schema.json` as design-only `$defs` and artifact families, including `test_capability_report`, `test_harness_probe_report`, `test_strategy`, `test_case`, `test_run_receipt`, and `visual_evidence`. These names are schema definitions inside the single plans-to-code handoff schema draft; they are not separate runtime queues or emitted product artifacts.

items.title: Testing command catalog seam has no declared consumer or ContractRef
items.statement: The core requires six cmd.testing rows, but the consumer and integration lists omit UI_Command_Catalog and no ContractRef binds command payloads, handlers, authorization checks, or receipt projections to the testing policy owner.
items.impact: Commands can exist in prose without a compiling owner/consumer path, leaving the GUI controls unwired or semantically divergent.

evidence.exact_quote: The required command rows are `cmd.testing.capability_policy.set`, `cmd.testing.visibility_policy.set`, `cmd.testing.session.open`, `cmd.testing.session.watch`, `cmd.testing.session.background`, and `cmd.testing.session.redaction.inspect`. Each command must produce receipt evidence linked to the effective policy snapshot, visible-session identity, artifact/evidence refs, redaction profile, currentness/revalidation result, and fallback route when a visual surface cannot be embedded.

Integration surfaces:
- `Plans/Plan_To_Node_Compilation.md` consumes capability and binding requirements while drafting future non-executable NodeSeed candidates, WorkGraph drafts, and WorkNode requests after the compiler contract exists.
- `Plans/Executor_Protocol.md` consumes test binding and receipt contracts at intake, dispatch, verification, repair, and certification boundaries.
- `Plans/Tools.md` owns concrete browser, GUI, device, CLI, and project-native test helpers.
- `Plans/Project_Output_Artifacts.md` and `Plans/Runtime_Artifacts_Panel.md` project test artifacts and evidence without becoming test policy owners.
- `Plans/FinalGUISpec.md` may show visible testing capability and evidence state, but it does not re-own automated-testing policy.

items.title: Visible states can present stale or contradictory truth
items.statement: The projection list has visibility modes and receipts mention currentness, but the core does not require loading, stale, reconnecting, superseded, failed-command, receipt-pending, or policy-changed-during-run states, nor precedence when several apply.
items.impact: A detached or backgrounded session can display an old pass against a newly changed policy or failed revalidation.

evidence.exact_quote: Acceptance coverage must prove effective-policy receipts, visible-session receipts, TestRunReceipt linkage, Open/Watch fallback behavior, background continuation, disabled reason projection, and redaction-before-display/persistence. PMConcept browser/terminal/testing demos are `concept_fixture_only` until those receipts and wiring rows exist.

items.title: Operational observability is reduced to captured test output
items.statement: Logs, console, and network artifacts are evidence payloads, but there is no health/latency/error telemetry for discovery, adapters, session control, redaction, artifact persistence, or receipt linkage, and no correlation or support-bundle contract.
items.impact: Operators cannot distinguish product-pipeline failure from project test failure or trace a broken receipt across components.

evidence.exact_quote: Browser and GUI automation manifests must carry `browser_session_id`, PM-native browser runtime state, visibility state, Open/Watch state, `runtime_unavailable` remediation actions, PageRepresentation refs, screenshot/PDF/console/network artifact refs, and redaction manifest refs. Playwright/CDP may appear only as fallback or reference test-driver evidence; PM-managed native browser sessions are the product runtime identity. Negative fixtures cover no-browser/runtime-unavailable, hidden prompt-injection chips, redaction failure, no-network denial, SSRF/private-host denial, robots/fanout/depth denial, cache hit/miss/TTL, and partial crawl/research/source citation outcomes.

items.title: Conditional evidence clauses have no machine-verifiable omission reason
items.statement: The phrases where supported and where available and permitted leave it unknown how omitted evidence is distinguished from unsupported capability, denied authority, adapter failure, or an implementation shortcut; no mandatory reason code or negative proof is specified.
items.impact: A verification path may silently omit the modality that would have exposed a defect while still appearing compliant.

evidence.exact_quote: Visible testing projections must include `show_when_possible`, visible active, collapsed, detached, backgrounded, and non-embeddable states. Web evidence must show browser navigation, clicks, form input, assertions, screenshots, console, network, and pass/fail progression where supported. Native evidence must show Swift/live preview, hot reload, simulator, emulator, physical device stream, application window, interaction trace, screenshots, and logs where available and permitted.

items.title: Missing discovery evidence explicitly blocks readiness
items.statement: The core explicitly prevents a guessed runner from becoming test-ready when discovery evidence is missing.

evidence.exact_quote: - Missing discovery evidence blocks test-ready status instead of guessing a runner.

items.title: Production dev/test capabilities default off
items.statement: The core explicitly prevents dev/test and browser automation controls from leaking into production without configuration and permission/audit receipts.

evidence.exact_quote: The Slint/WASM web GUI development workflow uses a trusted local daemon plus a static web route, fixture mode, browser automation smoke tests, screenshots/state capture, deterministic state hooks, and fast rebuild/reload loops. The test harness must prove daemon capability probes, pairing/origin/CSRF protections, degraded reasons when the daemon is absent or narrowed, screenshot and state-capture evidence, and reload behavior for the static web route. Production builds must not enable dev/test, MCP, live-preview, fixture, or browser automation controls unless explicit configuration enables the capability and records permission/audit receipts.

items.title: Manual-only completion is explicitly forbidden
items.statement: The core establishes that missing automated verification blocks or defers work and cannot be replaced by human eyeballing.

evidence.exact_quote: WorkNode completion cannot require human eyeballing. Tests, smoke checks, app launch, browser sessions, GUI/device sessions, screenshots, logs, and evidence capture run automatically where required. If Puppet Master cannot automatically verify a WorkNode after the compiler/runtime boundary is explicitly enabled, it must record a test capability blocker or deferred non-executable test-harness WorkNode request candidate rather than silently passing. For web projects, once the native product is built, Puppet Master built-in browser automation is the primary native web test automation path; Playwright can be optional, fallback, or project-native, not the native default.

items.title: Contract readiness does not falsely enable runtime
items.statement: The core clearly separates contract-source readiness from executable compiler/runtime readiness.

evidence.exact_quote: The Automated Testing System is ready as a contract source for future Plan-to-node compilation, but it does not make the compiler executable. Current node readiness remains `runtime_disabled` until `Plans/Plan_To_Node_Compilation.md` and a later explicit enablement allow runtime PlanCompile launch and node-artifact generation.

items.title: Browser threat cases have explicit negative fixtures
items.statement: The core explicitly calls for fixtures covering prompt injection, SSRF/private hosts, network denial, robots, fanout/depth, cache behavior, and partial outcomes.

evidence.exact_quote: Browser and GUI automation manifests must carry `browser_session_id`, PM-native browser runtime state, visibility state, Open/Watch state, `runtime_unavailable` remediation actions, PageRepresentation refs, screenshot/PDF/console/network artifact refs, and redaction manifest refs. Playwright/CDP may appear only as fallback or reference test-driver evidence; PM-managed native browser sessions are the product runtime identity. Negative fixtures cover no-browser/runtime-unavailable, hidden prompt-injection chips, redaction failure, no-network denial, SSRF/private-host denial, robots/fanout/depth denial, cache hit/miss/TTL, and partial crawl/research/source citation outcomes.

items.title: Redaction failure blocks silent evidence downgrade
items.statement: The core explicitly makes redaction precede display and persistence and prevents an unrecorded downgrade when redaction fails.

evidence.exact_quote: Screenshots, videos, logs, console output, network traces, and artifact previews apply secret and sensitive-data redaction before display or persistence. Redaction failures block display/persistence until resolved or explicitly authorized by the owning policy; they do not silently downgrade evidence quality.

dimension_assessments.summary: The required cmd.testing surface lacks an explicit catalog/handler consumer binding.
Policy and visibility states are enumerated without legal transitions or precedence.
Policy updates and session commands lack versioning, idempotency, and ordering semantics.
Partial artifact and receipt production has no explicit terminal-state model.
Install and test-run failures lack rollback, resume, and cleanup contracts.
Production defaults are guarded, but actor binding and redaction override authority remain unspecified.
Redaction is required, but retention, deletion, propagation, and override lifecycle are absent.
Browser threat fixtures exist, but repository-supplied harness execution lacks a trust boundary.
Visible state can become stale or contradictory during async policy and session changes.
A no-network fixture exists for web work, but online-research-dependent capability discovery has no normative offline outcome.
Evidence streams have no bounded size, concurrency, quota, or backpressure policy.
Tested desktop apps may receive accessibility checks, but the testing GUI itself has no accessibility contract.
Visible testing states and remediation text have no localization behavior or oracle.
Artifact families lack versioning, negotiation, and migration semantics.
Captured application evidence is not a substitute for pipeline health and correlation telemetry.
Auto may install capabilities without preview, cancellation, rollback, or cleanup evidence.
The command surface is not bound to a catalog/handler contract, though other major consumers are named.
Manual-only completion is forbidden, but flaky retry outcomes and conditional evidence omission are not falsifiably governed.
Conditional evidence clauses permit unknown omissions unless machine-readable reason codes and negative proof are added.
